quizName: DMV Practice Test #4 20 Questions • Passing Score 16

questions.question: What should you do to reduce your chance of getting into an accident?

options.text: Try to blend in and not be noticed by other drivers.
Do not use turn signals unless you are driving at night.
Use your turn signals when changing lanes and turning.
Drive very close to the vehicle in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signals when changing lanes and turning.
questions.explanation: To reduce accident risk, other drivers need to see you. Tell them what you plan to do by using turn signals and brake lights. Keep space between you and other vehicles. Look ahead 12 seconds. Be ready if something dangerous happens.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you are:

options.text: Allowed to use the full width of a lane.
Required to share a lane with trucks.
Required to ride on the shoulder when there is one.
Allowed to ride on the sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allowed to use the full width of a lane.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need a full lane to ride safely, just like any other vehicle. Never share a lane with another vehicle.

questions.question: When should you inspect your motorcycle before riding?

options.text: Before every ride.
About once every 10 rides.
Once a month.
Once a season.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before every ride.
questions.explanation: Small problems on a motorcycle are more dangerous than on a car. Check your motorcycle before every ride to stay safe.

questions.question: Why should motorcycle riders turn their heads to look over their shoulders before changing lanes?

options.text: Motorcycles have blind spots like all vehicles.
Turning your head gets the attention of other drivers.
Mirrors are not very useful.
You should make eye contact with nearby drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles have blind spots like all vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots that mirrors cannot show. Always turn your head to check for vehicles or hazards in your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: Shifting to a lower gear has an effect similar to:

options.text: Using the brakes.
Speeding up.
Swerving.
Turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using the brakes.
questions.explanation: Shifting to a lower gear slows your motorcycle, like using the brakes. This is called engine braking.

questions.question: Which surface provides good traction?

options.text: Wet pavement
Dry pavement
Lane markings
Snow

questions.correctAnswerText: Dry pavement
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, and painted lane markings all provide poor traction. Dry pavement gives the best grip for your tires.

questions.question: Taking corners too fast:

options.text: Can cause you to cross into another lane.
Is better than going too slowly.
Usually keeps you in your lane.
Is okay because motorcycles are small.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can cause you to cross into another lane.
questions.explanation: Going too fast around a corner can make you cross into another lane or leave the road. Slow down before you turn.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Speed up and lean the motorcycle.
Speed up and keep the motorcycle upright.
Slow down and lean the motorcycle.
Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid a slippery surface, keep your motorcycle upright and go as slowly as possible across it.

questions.question: How does your body remove alcohol?

options.text: Through time.
By drinking coffee.
By exercising.
By taking a cold shower.

questions.correctAnswerText: Through time.
questions.explanation: Your body needs time to remove alcohol. There is no fast way to become sober.

questions.question: What is the correct body position on a motorcycle?

options.text: Sit forward enough so your arms are slightly bent when holding the grips.
Sit as far back as possible and stretch to reach the grips.
Lean forward so your arms hold you up.
Keep your knees far from the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit forward enough so your arms are slightly bent when holding the grips.
questions.explanation: Sit forward enough that your arms are slightly bent when holding the grips. This lets you easily reach and use the controls.

questions.question: When riding, you should:

options.text: Always look ahead and watch for danger.
Watch the controls and speedometer instead of the road.
Not worry about hazards because there are very few on the road.
Look ahead but try not to look for hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always look ahead and watch for danger.
questions.explanation: Always look far ahead while riding. This helps you see problems before you reach them and gives you time to react.

questions.question: Which surface gives a motorcycle the best grip?

options.text: A gravel road
Dry pavement
Mud
Lane markings

questions.correctAnswerText: Dry pavement
questions.explanation: Many surfaces are slippery for motorcycles. Wet pavement, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal plates in the road are all more dangerous than dry pavement.

questions.question: Riding next to a car:

options.text: Is a good idea.
Can put you in the driver's blind spot.
Is only a problem if the road is wet.
Makes it easier for the other driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can put you in the driver's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding directly next to another vehicle is dangerous. The driver may not see you in their blind spot. Also, the vehicle blocks your escape route if you need to avoid danger.

questions.question: Why is it dangerous to ride directly next to another vehicle?

options.text: You may be in its blind spot.
It is distracting to have a vehicle next to you.
Other drivers may want to use the lane.
It would be hard to see behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in its blind spot.
questions.explanation: The driver may not see you in their blind spot. Also, if another hazard appears, the vehicle blocks your way to escape.

questions.question: What is the best footwear for a motorcycle rider?

options.text: Sturdy boots
Tennis shoes
Shoes with loose laces
Sandals

questions.correctAnswerText: Sturdy boots
questions.explanation: Sturdy boots or high shoes that support your ankles offer the best protection. High-top laced boots are best. If your laces are long, tuck them in before riding.

questions.question: About blind spots on motorcycles:

options.text: Motorcycles do not have blind spots because they are small.
Motorcycles have blind spots, but they are too small to worry about.
Motorcycles have blind spots that you should check regularly.
Motorcycles are too small to have blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles have blind spots that you should check regularly.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots just like any vehicle. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes. Make head checks part of your normal scanning routine.

questions.question: When should you inspect your motorcycle?

options.text: Before every ride.
Once a week.
Once a month.
Once a season.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before every ride.
questions.explanation: Always inspect your motorcycle before you ride. Small problems are more serious on a motorcycle than on a car.

questions.question: How can you make your motorcycle easier to see?

options.text: Attach a large flag to it.
Keep your headlight on.
Wave at other drivers.
Ride on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your headlight on.
questions.explanation: Wear bright, reflective clothing. Keep your headlight on at all times. Use your turn signals and brake light properly.

questions.question: Where should you find information about your specific motorcycle?

options.text: The owner's manual.
A general book about motorcycles.
Someone with a different type of motorcycle.
A television show about motorcycle riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: The owner's manual.
questions.explanation: Read the owner's manual before riding your motorcycle for the first time. This is especially important if you are riding a borrowed motorcycle.

questions.question: If you feel tired while riding, you should:

options.text: Keep riding and hope you wake up.
Ride faster.
Ride on the shoulder.
Stop and rest.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest.
questions.explanation: Do not ride if you are tired. On long trips, take a rest break every two hours to avoid fatigue.
